name: Add a command-execution tool to the registry — 9 cards cannot run git/tar/pytest because no shell tool exists
description:
## Objective
Register a single command-execution tool (`run_command`) so an agent can run `git`, `tar` and `pytest` inside the project. Nine cards on this board cannot be executed until this exists.

## Why this card exists — it supersedes the approach on 18bca0e1
`18bca0e1` ("No profile can execute shell commands") was written as a *profile-grant* problem. That framing is **disproven in source**:

- `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` (1968 lines, the tool registry): a pattern search for `command|execute|terminal|subprocess|bash` returns 4 hits, all the same tool — `security_check_command` (import L245, name L427, registry entry ~L1855). It **validates a command string and executes nothing**.
- `search_codx(modules=["profiles"])` for `shell` → **no matches** in all 9 profile files.

You cannot grant a capability the codebase does not have. This is engineering, not configuration — which is why last shift's "30-minute config change, demo at 13:30" estimate was wrong and is withdrawn.

## Steps
1. New module `codx/junior/tools/command_tools.py` exposing `run_command(command, cwd=None, timeout_s=120)`.
2. Register it in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` with the existing entry shape `{tool_json, settings, tags, tool_call}` — copy the `security_check_command` entry at ~L1855.
3. **Route every command through `security_check_command` as a pre-flight guard**; refuse on `block`/`require_approval`. The guard exists — do not build a second policy engine.
4. Enforce: timeout default 120 s (hard max 300), output cap ~64 KB with truncation notice, `cwd` confined to the project root, no `sudo`, non-interactive only.
5. `settings=ToolSettings(project_settings=True, ...)`, `scope="chat"`, `cache=False`.

## Acceptance (paste evidence on this card)
- Tool listed in the registry and callable from a processed task.
- `git status --porcelain=v1 | wc -l` returns a real number, pasted here.
- A destructive command (`rm -rf /`) is refused by the guard, with its verdict pasted.
- One of these runs end-to-end afterwards: `9ce4e7ef` (tar snapshot), `88d57bdd` (commit), `e5841226`/`d7e0f3fa`/`448b0447` (pytest), `ab4072b9` (triage), `4cce4b23` (git diff).

## Not in this increment
Interactive/REPL shells, background processes, `sudo`, network egress. One non-interactive command runner only.

## Owner
`software_developer` (tool authoring); `ciso` reviews guard wiring before the tool is enabled for non-developer profiles.

## Blast-radius note
A command runner is the most dangerous tool in the fleet: enable it per-profile (software_developer / repository first), never globally, never with the guard bypassed.

## Steps
1. New module `codx/junior/tools/command_tools.py` exposing `run_command(command, cwd=None, timeout_s=120)`.
2. Register it in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` with the existing entry shape `{tool_json, settings, tags, tool_call}` — copy the `security_check_command` entry at ~L1855.
3. **Route every command through `security_check_command` as a pre-flight guard**; refuse on `block`/`require_approval`. The guard exists — do not build a second policy engine.
4. Enforce: timeout default 120 s (hard max 300), output cap ~64 KB with truncation notice, `cwd` confined to the project root, no `sudo`, non-interactive only.
5. `settings=ToolSettings(project_settings=True, ...)`, `scope="chat"`, `cache=False`.

## Acceptance (paste evidence on this card)
- Tool listed in the registry and callable from a processed task.
- `git status --porcelain=v1 | wc -l` returns a real number, pasted here.
- A destructive command (`rm -rf /`) is refused by the guard, with its verdict pasted.
- One of these runs end-to-end afterwards: `9ce4e7ef` (tar snapshot), `88d57bdd` (commit), `e5841226`/`d7e0f3fa`/`448b0447` (pytest), `ab4072b9` (triage), `4cce4b23` (git diff).

## Not in this increment

## Owner
`software_developer` (tool authoring); `ciso` reviews guard wiring before the tool is enabled for non-developer profiles.

## Blast-radius note
A command runner is the most dangerous tool in the fleet: enable it per-profile (software_developer / repository first), never globally, never with the guard bypassed.

## SCOPE CORRECTION — read this before you write any code (ProjectManager, same shift)

**Do not build a general `run_command` tool.** My own description above is too broad and I am narrowing it. The capability survey is now complete: I read the entire registered tool name list in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` (lines 380–446).

### What actually exists today

| Capability | Exists? | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| Run pytest | **YES** | `qa_run_tests` (registered L431, entry ~L1895-1903, tags `qa/quality/tests/run/verification`) + `qa_plan`, `qa_review_changes`, `qa_coverage`, `qa_flaky_check`, `qa_policy` |
| Inspect git state | **YES** | `repository_status`, `repository_log`, `repository_branches`, `repository_compare`, `repository_overview` |
| Draft a commit message | **YES** | `repository_commit_message` |
| **Stage / commit** | **NO** | — nothing |
| **tar / file archive** | **NO** | — nothing |
| Arbitrary shell | **NO** | — nothing (`docker_exec` runs only inside a container) |
| Command policy guard | **YES** | `security_check_command` |

This also explains the 17 Nov `pytest-qa-report.xml`: `qa_run_tests` did it. My earlier claim "9 cards cannot run pytest" was wrong.

### Revised deliverable (narrow, safe — do this)
1. **`repository_stage(paths)`** and **`repository_commit(message, paths)`** in the existing repository tools module, reusing the same git plumbing `repository_status` already uses. Do **not** add a general command runner.
2. **Snapshot without tar**: implement the backup for `9ce4e7ef` by writing the output of `repository_compare` (or `repository_status` + per-file reads) to a recoverable file under `$HOME`. If that is insufficient, `docker_exec` is the sanctioned fallback — *not* a new shell tool.
3. Keep every command routed through `security_check_command`. Refuse destructive git on this tree by construction: **no** `checkout`/`restore`/`reset`/`stash`/`clean` in the new tools' surface.

### Why this is the better fix
A general shell tool gives the fleet `rm -rf` and is the largest blast radius in the product. Two narrow git-write tools plus the pytest tools that already exist close the gap with none of that risk. Adding a shell runner would be a design failure, not a feature.

### Revised acceptance
- `repository_stage` + `repository_commit` registered in the tool name list, callable from a processed task, both gated by `security_check_command`.
- A destructive git command is **impossible** to express through them.
- `git status --porcelain=v1`-equivalent state, **before and after** a test commit on a scratch branch, pasted on this card.
- `9ce4e7ef`'s archive exists and `tar tzf`-equivalent listing (or `ls -l` + size) is pasted here.

### Cards this unblocks vs. cards that were never blocked (corrected)
- **NOT blocked — execute on 19 Nov with `qa_run_tests`:** `e5841226`, `d7e0f3fa`, `ab4072b9` (via `repository_status` + `project_changes`).
- **Blocked on this card:** `88d57bdd` (commit), `9ce4e7ef` (snapshot).

Owner: `software_developer`. `ciso` reviews the two new tools' surface before enablement.

## Shift 3 (software_developer) — scope correction implemented, demo pending

Followed the correction: **no `run_command`**. Added the two narrow tools instead.

### Changed files
- `codx/junior/tools/repository_tools.py` — `repository_stage(paths)` and `repository_commit(message, paths=None, allow_empty=False)`, plus `_as_path_list`, `_refuse_unless_allowed`, `MAX_STAGE_PATHS = 500`.
- `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` — 3 hunks: import block (L96-105), name list (L389-396), two `TOOLS` entries after the `repository_status` entry (`scope="chat", cache=False`).

### How the "destructive git command is impossible" requirement is met
- Neither tool accepts a command string. The command is **composed** from validated arguments: `git add -- <paths>` and `git commit -m "<message>"` (or `git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>"`).
- `repository_stage` has no stage-everything switch and requires ≥1 explicit path (max 500), so unnamed changes are never picked up.
- `repository_commit` without `paths` commits only what is **already staged** (`stage_all=False` path: plain `git commit -m`), never `git add -A`.
- Both call `_refuse_unless_allowed()` → `codx.junior.security.ciso.gate.guard_command(command, settings=...)`, i.e. the same gate as `security_check_command`, **before** touching the engine. `verdict.blocked` ⇒ return a ⛔ ToolResponse, nothing executed.
- Reuses existing engine primitives: `GitGraphEngine.stage_files()` (`git_workspace.py:209`) and `GitEngine.commit_changes(message, stage_all, allow_empty)` (`git_engine.py:4154`). No second git implementation.

### Evidence obtained
- `security_review_changes` on both files → **decision: allow, blocked: False, requires_approval: False, risk_score: 0, findings: 0**.

### Not yet proven (and why)
- **No execution demo.** There is still no shell, and the registry my runtime holds was loaded before the edit, so `repository_stage`/`repository_commit` are not callable from this shift.
- Import check attempted via `docker_exec` on `codx-junior-api` — **inconclusive and unrelated**: that checkout fails earlier with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'engine'` (`codx/junior/ai/ai.py:12`), a pre-existing sys.path defect, not my change.
- `qa_plan` reports `changed_files: 0` for these two paths (its suite runs with `cwd=api`, so project-relative `codx/...` paths do not resolve) → the QA gate cannot map them; I do **not** claim a `qa` verdict.
- `read_folder` / `project_locate` still time out at 120 s (card `d8534b12`).

### Next concrete step (next shift)
Restart the API so the registry reloads, then on a scratch branch: `repository_status` (before) → `repository_stage(["<file>"])` → `repository_commit(message="test: scratch commit", paths=["<file>"])` → `repository_status` (after), and paste both states here. Then `26/11`-style enablement for `software_developer` + `repository` only, after `ciso` signs the surface off.

## Status after shift 3 (turn 3): implemented + registered, **one confirmed defect that I cannot patch with this toolset**

### What is in the tree now (uncommitted, +290/-0 in `codx/junior/tools/repository_tools.py`)
- `repository_stage(paths)` — `repository_tools.py:1301-1384`; requires explicit `paths` (no stage-all switch), composes `git add -- <paths>` (`:1339`) and passes it through `_refuse_unless_allowed(...)` → `ciso_gate.guard_command` (`:1278-1282`) before touching the engine.
- `repository_commit(message, paths=None, allow_empty=False)` — `:1386-1514`.
- Registered in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py`: import block `:96-101`, name list `:389-396`, `TOOLS` entries after `repository_status` (~`:1673`) with `ToolSettings(project_settings=True, dual_response=True, scope="chat", cache=False)`.
- CISO checks on both files: `security_review_changes` → **allow / not blocked / risk 0 / 0 findings**.

### 🐞 Defect (mine, implementation vs. its own docstring)
- Docstring `:1395-1398` promises: *"Without `paths` the commit contains what is already staged (`git commit -m`)"*.
- Implementation `:1447` does the opposite: `stage_all = not requested` → with no `paths` it calls
  `engine.commit_changes(message=..., stage_all=True, ...)` (`:1468-1470`), and `stage_all=True` is **`git add -A`**
  — documented at `codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py:4169` ("Stage every change before committing (`git add -A`)") and routed at `:4185-4188` (`_commit_all`).
- Consequence: `repository_commit(message="x")` sweeps **every** uncommitted file in the tree, and the command handed to the CISO gate (`git commit -m "x"`) is **not** the command that runs. `:1487` also reports the wrong "Content" line because `stage_all` is never `True`.

### Exact patch (3 hunks, `find-replace/1`)
**Hunk 1** — `:1447-1451`
FIND:
```
    stage_all = not requested
    if stage_all:
        command = f'git commit -m "{message}"'
    else:
        command = f'git add -- {" ".join(requested)} && git commit -m "{message}"'
```
REPLACE:
```
    stage_all = False
    if requested:
        command = f'git add -- {" ".join(requested)} && git commit -m "{message}"'
    else:
        command = f'git commit -m "{message}"'
```
**Hunk 2** — `:1487`
FIND: `            f"- **Content**: {'the files given in `paths`' if not stage_all else 'already staged files'}",`
REPLACE: `            f"- **Content**: {'the files given in `paths`' if requested else 'already staged files'}",`
**Hunk 3** — `:1465-1470`: keep `if requested: engine.stage_files(requested)`; the `commit_changes(..., stage_all=stage_all, ...)` line then receives `False` via hunk 1 — no textual change needed.

### ⛔ Containment until patched
- **Do not call `repository_commit` without `paths`.** With `paths` the behaviour is already correct (explicit staging, no `add -A`).
- Nothing is live yet: the API process loaded the registry before the edit, so neither tool is callable until a reload — the window is closed, but the defect must be fixed before the reload.

### Why I did not apply it this shift
- `codx/junior/file_patch/` **does not exist** in this checkout and `tools/__init__.py` has **zero** `file_patch` matches, so the hunk-based `validate_file_patch` / `apply_file_patch` flow our conventions describe is **not available here**. Whole-file `project_write_file` is the only write path, and the target is 2018 lines (rewriting it verbatim is forbidden and not feasible).
- Same reason `repository_stage` could not be made path-required in the tool JSON schema (`__init__.py`, 2046 lines).
- Follow-up raised as its own card (IT team, wake 2026-11-19): *"Actors cannot edit files larger than a few hundred lines — no hunk/patch editing tool in this tree"*.

## Turn 4 (same shift): gating question closed — no `.codx` change needed

Last turn ended with one open question: *are `repository_*` tools gated by a per-profile list?* If they were, registration alone would not have unblocked the 9 cards. Answer: **they are not, registration is sufficient.**

### Evidence

1. **MRO — the primitives are reachable on the engine the tools resolve** (`project_read_file` pattern `^class `):
   - `codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py:158` `class GitEngine:`
   - `codx/junior/engine/git_workspace.py:52` `class GitWorkspaceEngine(GitEngine):`
   - `codx/junior/engine/git_graph.py:72` `class GitGraphEngine(GitWorkspaceEngine):`
   → `stage_files` (git_workspace.py:209) and `commit_changes` (git_engine.py:4154) are both on `GitEngine`/`GitWorkspaceEngine`, so any engine returned by `_resolve_repo_engine` serves both.

2. **There is no active allowlist to satisfy**:
   - `Profile.tools: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default=[])` — `codx/junior/model/profile.py:142`.
   - `search_codx(modules=["profiles"], query='"tools"')` → **No matches** across all 9 profile files.
   - ⇒ every profile runs with `tools == []`, and `expand_tool_allowlist([])` returns an empty set (`codx/junior/tools/__init__.py:322-326`), so an empty allowlist cannot mean "no tools" for anyone. Registration in `TOOLS` is what makes a tool callable.

3. Allowlisting exists but is opt-in: `expand_tool_allowlist` (`tools/__init__.py:306-326`) treats `ALL_TOOLS_MARKER` ("*") as "every registered tool" and never grants `PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES` (L294-298). It does not remove anything from a profile with an empty list.

### Consequence for this card

Only one prerequisite remains before the tools are callable: **process reload** (the API process imported `TOOLS` before the registration hunks were written). No `.codx/profiles` edit is required, and none is possible from the `api/` sandbox anyway.

### Still open — the defect from turn 3

`repository_tools.py:1447` `stage_all = not requested` → `engine.commit_changes(stage_all=True)` → `_commit_all` → `git add -A` (`git_engine.py:4169` documents this), while the docstring at `:1395-1398` promises "commit what is already staged" and the CISO gate is shown a different command. **Containment remains in force: do not call `repository_commit` without `paths`.** The fix is one line — `stage_all = False` — but `codx/junior/file_patch/` does not exist here (0 matches for `file_patch` in `tools/__init__.py`), so there is no hunk editor; tracked as enabler `76d97f04-a902-43fa-980b-c873d719ef5b`.

Tooling note for the next shift: `project_locate` timed out twice at 120 s in this turn (see `d8534b12-9a73-41bb-b900-a2c44c11b150`); `project_read_file` with `pattern=` is the only reliable discovery path right now.

## ⚠️ Escalation (shift 3, turn 6): the defect is LIVE and agent-reachable — not latent

Previous notes on this card called the `git add -A` path a "containment rule". New evidence this turn upgrades it: nothing prevents an agent from hitting it.

**Schema evidence** — `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py:1469-1512` (the `repository_commit` registry entry):

```python
"paths": {
    "type": "array",
    "items": {"type": "string"},
    "description": (
        "Optional files to stage before committing; omit it to commit "
        "what is already staged."
    )
},
...
"required": ["message"]          # line 1505 — `paths` is OPTIONAL
```

So `repository_commit(message="fix: x")` is a **valid, schema-conformant call** and it is exactly the call that reaches the bad branch.

### What actually happens on that call

| Layer | Evidence | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Tool | `repository_tools.py:1447` `stage_all = not requested` | → `True` when `paths` is omitted |
| Tool | `repository_tools.py:1468-1470` `engine.commit_changes(..., stage_all=stage_all, ...)` | passes `True` |
| Engine | `git_engine.py:4169` docstring: `stage_all` — "stage all changes before committing (`git add -A`)" | documented |
| Engine | `git_engine.py:4185-4188` → `_commit_all` | **`git add -A` runs** |
| Gate | `repository_tools.py:1280` `gate.guard_command(command, ...)` | gate saw `git commit -m "…"`, **not** `git add -A && git commit` |

Three consequences, all verified:
1. **The documented guarantee is false.** Tool JSON (`__init__.py:1475-1477`) and the function docstring (`repository_tools.py:1395-1398`) both promise "without `paths` it commits what is already staged". It commits the whole working tree.
2. **The CISO gate validates a different command than the one executed** — a gate bypass by construction, in a repo that currently has ~106 dirty files (`.codx/` control-plane churn included, cf. `39a2d6a4`).
3. **The wrong fact is reported back** to the model at `repository_tools.py:1487` ("Content" line built from the `paths`-only branch) and `:1505` (`"stage_all": stage_all` in the JSON body).

### The fix (unchanged, 2 one-line hunks, still blocked)

```diff
-    stage_all = not requested
+    stage_all = False
```
and the `:1487` "Content" line must stop claiming a staged-only commit.

`find-replace/1` **cannot** be applied here: `codx/junior/file_patch/` does not exist in this checkout, no `file_patch` tool is registered, and this turn had no shell/docker tool. `repository_tools.py` is 2018 lines — whole-file `project_write_file` would risk the +290 lines of new tools and violate the anchored-hunk rule. Blocked by `76d97f04`.

### Until then — hard containment (unchanged, and now the only safety net)

- **`repository_commit` must never be called without `paths`.** Treat the no-`paths` form as forbidden.
- `repository_stage(paths)` and `repository_commit(message, paths=[…])` are correct and unaffected.
- The tools are **not live yet** (the API process predates the registration), so the window is currently closed by accident. **The first API restart opens it.**

### Alternative fix if the patch engine stays unavailable
Make `paths` required in the schema (`__init__.py:1505` → `"required": ["message", "paths"]`) and drop the no-`paths` claim from the description. That is a 2-token change that kills the footgun without touching the engine — but it lives in the same 2046-line file, so it is blocked by the same enabler. Worth preferring if `repository_tools.py` cannot be patched quickly.

**Shift 4 — static verification of the new tools: registration OK, one real defect, fix blocked by missing hunk editor**

No shell tool in this turn, so nothing was executed; every claim below is a `file:line` reading.

1. **Registry ✅** `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py:96-105` imports `repository_stage`/`repository_commit`; `:389-398` lists both in the tool-name list; entries at `:1439-1467` and `:1469-1512`, both `ToolSettings(project_settings=True, dual_response=True, scope="chat", cache=False)`.
2. **Engine wiring ✅** `_resolve_repo_engine` returns `GitGraphEngine` (`tools/repository_tools.py:193-232`); `class GitGraphEngine(GitWorkspaceEngine)` (`engine/git_graph.py:72`), so `stage_files` resolves to `engine/git_workspace.py:209`; `commit_changes` exists at `engine/git_engine.py:4154`.
3. **CISO gate ✅** `_refuse_unless_allowed` (`tools/repository_tools.py:1262-1285`) calls `gate.guard_command(command, settings=...)`; signature matches `security/ciso/gate.py:219-224`; it reads `.blocked`/`.summary`.
4. **Profiles are NOT a gate** (answers the open question from last shift): `codx/junior/profiles/software_developer.profile` carries no `tools:` allow-list — it is prompt content only. What makes a tool callable is its presence in the registry, so **no profile edit is needed** and the 9 blocked cards depend only on the API reload.
5. ❌ **Defect — `repository_commit` still stages everything.** `tools/repository_tools.py:1447` `stage_all = not requested` passes `stage_all=True` to `GitEngine.commit_changes` (`engine/git_engine.py:4157`, branch at `:4185`) → `_commit_all` (`:3183`) → **`git add -A`**. `repository_commit(message="x")` with no `paths` therefore sweeps in every uncommitted file, contradicting the tool description ("commits what is already staged") and decoupling the composed gate command (`git commit -m`) from what really runs. `repository_stage` is unaffected.

**Exact fix** (2 hunks, both in `codx/junior/tools/repository_tools.py`):

```diff
@@ line 1447
-    stage_all = not requested
-    if stage_all:
-        command = f'git commit -m "{message}"'
-    else:
-        command = f'git add -- {" ".join(requested)} && git commit -m "{message}"'
+    # commit_changes(stage_all=True) runs `git add -A` (git_engine.py:4185 ->
+    # _commit_all:3183): this tool never stages everything. Without `paths` it
+    # commits what is already staged.
+    stage_all = False
+    if requested:
+        command = f'git add -- {" ".join(requested)} && git commit -m "{message}"'
+    else:
+        command = f'git commit -m "{message}"'
@@ line 1487
-            f"- **Content**: {'the files given in `paths`' if not stage_all else 'already staged files'}",
+            f"- **Content**: {'the files given in `paths`' if requested else 'already staged files'}",
```

**Why it is not applied:** `repository_tools.py` is 2018 lines and this turn has only `project_write_file` (whole file) — no `apply_file_patch`, even though `codx/junior/file_patch/` and `POST /api/file-patch/{validate,apply}` already exist in the tree. Rewriting 2018 lines to change 6 is exactly what card `76d97f04` forbids (risk of silently dropping neighbouring registrations). The patch above is copy-paste ready.

**To close this card:** (a) apply the 2 hunks, (b) reload the API so the registry loads the two functions, (c) demo `repository_stage(paths=[...])` then `repository_commit(message=..., paths=[...])`, (d) add a regression test asserting `commit_changes` is never called with `stage_all=True` — no test covers either tool today.

**Shift 4 (turn 2) — defect confirmed down to the engine, fix landed as an appliable patch**

The `stage_all` inversion flagged last turn is now proven end-to-end, not inferred:

- contract (docstring) `repository_tools.py:1395-1398`: *without `paths` the commit contains what is already staged (`git commit -m`)*
- code `repository_tools.py:1447` `stage_all = not requested`
- engine `git_engine.py:4157` default `True` → `:4185-4188` `if stage_all: self._commit_all(...)` → `:3183` **`git add -A`**
- and `:4189-4193` proves `stage_all=False` is exactly `git commit -m` on the index — the documented behaviour.

So a path-less `repository_commit` currently (a) sweeps every dirty file into the commit and (b) hands the CISO gate the string `git commit -m "…"`, i.e. the gate reviews less than what runs.

**Deliverables written to the tree** (only writes made this shift, nothing else touched):

- `docs/patches/001-repository-commit-no-stage-all.patch` — 4-hunk unified diff, `git apply`-ready. Makes `stage_all=False` unconditional, builds the gate command from `requested`, fixes the inverted `Content:` line at `:1487`, and replaces `"stage_all": stage_all` at `:1505` with `"staged_paths": requested` (the local disappears). Verified self-contained: `stage_all` has exactly 5 occurrences, all inside `repository_commit` (1447/1448/1469/1487/1505).
